intro: A checkpoint records a contiguous prefix of completed work. Concurrent workers may finish later items while an earlier item is still missing.
task: Advance a contiguous completed offset only across gap-free acknowledged sequence IDs.
requirements: committed is the largest contiguous processed sequence ID, an integer from -1 to 1000000000. acknowledged contains integer IDs from 0 to 1000000000, with duplicates allowed. Advance committed while each next ID is present. Return committed and sorted unique pending IDs greater than the new committed; ignore acknowledgments at or below the initial committed.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Membership in a set handles duplicate and out-of-order acknowledgments.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Never jump directly to the largest acknowledged ID; gaps must remain uncommitted.

explanation: A checkpoint records a contiguous prefix of completed work. Concurrent workers may finish later items while an earlier item is still missing.
Keeping later acknowledgments pending allows the frontier to advance once the gap closes. Ignoring old acknowledgments makes replayed completion events harmless.
